boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UNT rituals and spirit fixtures, from the Talons’ bonfire work to the class-ring fountain celebration.

cards.title: Homecoming Bonfire
cards.subtitle: Talons tradition · Homecoming week
cards.notes: View the bonfire only from designated event areas and follow event staff directions; Talons build it during the week before the Homecoming football game.
cards.short_summary: A Talons-built pallet bonfire burned the night before UNT’s Homecoming football game.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT Student Affairs says Talons have been entrusted with the Homecoming Bonfire since 1960 and build it during the week before it is burned.
cards.access_notes: Event-based; observe from designated public viewing areas and follow current Homecoming instructions.

cards.title: Spot the Spirit Flags
cards.subtitle: Talons tradition · Games and spirit marches
cards.notes: Look for the flags at the end zone near the cannon or at the front of a spirit march; enjoy the display without entering restricted field areas.
cards.short_summary: Talons safeguard and display UNT spirit flags at games, special events, and spirit marches.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT Student Affairs identifies the Talons as protectors of the Spirit Flags and says they use them at football games, basketball games, special events, and spirit marches.
cards.access_notes: View during scheduled games, special events, or spirit marches; field and event access rules apply.

cards.title: Find the Mean Green Machine
cards.subtitle: Talons’ 1931 Ford Model A Tudor Sedan
cards.notes: Watch for the green Model A at a home football game, spirit march, or special event, and admire it from the public route or viewing area.
cards.short_summary: A historic Ford Model A, protected and driven by Talons, makes ceremonial UNT appearances.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT Student Affairs describes the Mean Green Machine as a 1929 Ford Model A Tudor Sedan built in 1931 that Talons protect and drive at home football games, spirit marches, and special occasions.
cards.access_notes: Appearance is event-dependent; view from public spectator areas and do not approach the vehicle route.

cards.title: Hear Boomer the Cannon
cards.subtitle: UNT football tradition · Talons
cards.notes: If attending a home game, expect ceremonial cannon reports at key moments; use hearing protection and follow stadium staff directions during firing.
cards.short_summary: Talons fire a Mexican-American War replica cannon at designated moments of UNT home football games.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT Student Affairs says Talons use Boomer, a Mexican-American War replica, to signal touchdowns, kickoff, halftime, and the end of UNT home football games.
cards.access_notes: Occurs at scheduled UNT home football games and special moments; stadium admission and safety rules may apply.

cards.title: See McConnell Tower Glow Green
cards.subtitle: Post-victory tradition · Hurley Administration Building
cards.notes: After a varsity win, look toward McConnell Tower and join the public celebration from campus walkways; check Talons updates for the occasion.
cards.short_summary: McConnell Tower is lit green following North Texas varsity victories.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT Student Affairs says McConnell Tower is lit green after North Texas varsity team victories, with Talons leading post-football-game victory marches there.
cards.access_notes: The lighting follows varsity victories and special occasions; viewing from public campus areas is event-dependent.

cards.title: Watch the Flag Run
cards.subtitle: DATCU Stadium · Home football games
cards.notes: From the stands, watch Talons run the NORTH TEXAS flags after touchdowns and the Eagle flag after field goals; stay in spectator areas.
cards.short_summary: A 2013 Talons tradition pairs scoring plays with a run of UNT’s flags.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT Student Affairs says Talons have run NORTH TEXAS flags after touchdowns and the Eagle flag after field goals at DATCU Stadium since fall 2013.
cards.access_notes: Occurs during scheduled UNT home football games at DATCU Stadium; stadium admission and spectator rules apply.

cards.title: Eagle Ring Dive
cards.subtitle: Library Mall fountains · Commencement tradition
cards.notes: Eligible ring recipients can follow the UNT Ring Program’s semester instructions; observers should respect the ceremony setup and fountain-area guidance.
cards.short_summary: Graduates ceremonially submerge class rings as part of UNT’s pre-commencement ring celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT says the Eagle Ring Dive was added in 2018 and participating students submerge their rings during the Ring Ceremony celebration.
cards.access_notes: Held before commencement; participation details are sent to students who purchase rings in that semester.

cards.title: Make the Eagle Claw
cards.subtitle: University-wide UNT pride sign
cards.notes: Use the Eagle Claw when cheering with the Mean Green: make a V with your pointer and middle fingers, then curl your hand toward your palm.
cards.short_summary: UNT’s eagle-shaped hand sign is the university’s visual signal of pride and unity.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT’s Fall 2024 commencement program calls the Eagle Claw the university’s universal sign of pride and unity and provides its formation steps.
cards.source_title: Commencement Program for University of North Texas, Fall 2024
cards.access_notes: A hand-sign tradition that can be used in appropriate public cheering and photo settings.

cards.title: Wear Green on Friday
cards.subtitle: University-wide weekly pride tradition
cards.notes: Wear green on Friday if you want to take part in the campus-wide show of pride; any green item works, from a shirt to a small accessory.
cards.short_summary: UNT community members mark Fridays by wearing green throughout the year.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT Student Affairs’ Eagle Camp traditions material says students, faculty, staff, alumni, and other Mean Green fans wear green every Friday to show university pride.
cards.access_notes: A voluntary, year-round tradition; no event registration is indicated.

cards.entity_name: Green Brigade March to the Stadium and Fifth Quarter Performance
cards.title: Catch the Green Brigade’s Fifth Quarter
cards.subtitle: UNT Marching Band · Home football tradition
cards.notes: Check the football and band schedules, then stay in approved spectator areas after a home game to watch the Green Brigade’s Fifth Quarter performance.
cards.short_summary: UNT formally lists the Green Brigade’s march to the stadium and postgame Fifth Quarter as a spirit tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT’s History and Traditions page lists the Green Brigade March to the Stadium and Fifth Quarter Performance among its traditions of spirit.
cards.access_notes: Tied to scheduled home football activities; confirm game-day programming and follow stadium rules.
